items.followUp: A body weighing 15 N is raised vertically through 4 m. Calculate the potential energy stored in it.

rubric.why: Checks recognition of the given weight and height.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the weight as 20 N and height as 6 m.

rubric.why: The correct relation is needed to calculate gravitational potential energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct formula.

rubric.why: Checks correct substitution of the given values.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for substituting 20 N and 6 m into the formula.

rubric.why: The energy is the product of weight and vertical height, expressed in joules.
rubric.description: Calculates and gives the answer with unit.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for 120 J; award 1 mark if the numerical answer is correct but the unit is missing.

modelAnswer: Given: Weight, W = 20 N; height, h = 6 m.
Formula: P.E. = W × h.
Substitution: P.E. = 20 N × 6 m.

items.followUp: State Pascal’s Law and explain how a hydraulic jack multiplies force.

rubric.why: Pascal’s Law describes the transmission of applied pressure through an enclosed fluid.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for stating that pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished in all directions; award 1 mark for a substantially correct but incomplete statement.

rubric.why: The hydraulic press works because the transmitted pressure acts on a larger output-piston area to produce a larger force.
rubric.description: Explains the working of a hydraulic press.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for explaining that pressure from the small piston is transmitted through the fluid to the large piston, producing a larger output force; award 1 mark for a partially correct explanation.

modelAnswer: Pascal’s Law: Pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished in all directions and acts equally on every part of the fluid and the walls of its container.
A hydraulic press consists of two pistons of different areas connected by an enclosed liquid.
When a force F₁ is applied to the smaller piston of area A₁, it produces pressure P = F₁/A₁ in the liquid.
This pressure is transmitted equally to the larger piston of area A₂, so F₂/A₂ = F₁/A₁.
Since A₂ is larger than A₁, the output force F₂ is greater than the applied force F₁.

items.followUp: How many significant figures are in 450.0 m? Express the value in scientific notation.

rubric.why: The trailing zero is significant because the number is written with a decimal point.
rubric.description: Finds the number of significant figures.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that 210.0 has four significant figures.

rubric.why: The scientific notation must preserve all four significant figures and the original unit.
rubric.description: Writes the value in scientific notation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 2.100 × 10² g.

modelAnswer: 210.0 g has 4 significant figures.
In scientific notation: 210.0 g = 2.100 × 10² g.

items.followUp: Define a vector and give two examples.

rubric.why: A scalar is described by magnitude only and has no direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining a scalar as a quantity with magnitude only (no direction).

rubric.why: Examples must be scalar quantities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two correct scalar examples, such as mass, time, distance, speed, or temperature.

modelAnswer: A scalar is a physical quantity that has magnitude only and no direction.
Examples: mass and time.

items.followUp: Define acceleration and write its mathematical formula.

rubric.why: Velocity is defined as displacement per unit time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition in terms of displacement and time.

rubric.why: The formula expresses velocity as displacement divided by time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct velocity formula.

modelAnswer: Velocity is the displacement of a body per unit time.
Formula: v = s/t, where s is displacement and t is time.

items.followUp: What is the difference between balanced and unbalanced forces?

rubric.why: Like forces act along parallel lines in the same direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that like forces act in the same direction.

rubric.why: Unlike forces act along parallel lines in opposite directions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that unlike forces act in opposite directions.

modelAnswer: Like forces act in the same direction.
Unlike forces act in opposite directions.

items.followUp: Calculate the centripetal force on a 2 kg body moving at 4 m s⁻¹ in a circle of radius 2 m.

rubric.why: The radius must be converted from centimetres to metres before substitution.
rubric.description: Identifies the given data in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying m = 0.5 kg, r = 0.50 m, and v = 3 m s⁻¹.

rubric.why: This is the formula for centripetal force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

rubric.why: Checks substitution of the given quantities into the formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct substitution.

rubric.why: The calculation gives a centripetal force of 9 newtons.
rubric.description: Calculates the force and gives its unit.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for 9 N; award 1 mark for the correct numerical result without a unit.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 0.5 kg; r = 50 cm = 0.50 m; v = 3 m s⁻¹.
Formula: Fᶜ = mv²/r.
Substitution: Fᶜ = (0.5 kg)(3 m s⁻¹)²/(0.50 m).
Fᶜ = 9 kg m s⁻².
Answer: Fᶜ = 9 N.
